source.extractionPreview:
Social and Political Life
100
Chapter 8
Do you recall the 'Story of a shirt' from your Class VII
book? We saw there that a chain of markets links the
producer of cotton to the buyer of the shirt in the
supermarket. Buying and selling was taking place at
every step in the chain.
Many of the people directly or indirectly involved in
the production of the shirt - the small farmer producing
cotton, the weavers of Erode or the workers in the
garment - exporting factory - faced exploitation or an

activities.subject: Social
activities.question: Explain the main idea of Chapter 8.
activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.

correctItems.text: We saw there that a chain of markets links the producer of cotton to the buyer of the shirt in the supermarket.
Buying and selling was taking place at every step in the chain.
Markets everywhere tend to be exploitative of people - whether as workers, consumers or producers.
To protect people from such exploitation, the government makes certain laws.

distractors.text: Chapter 8 should be answered without using chapter facts.
An unrelated statement can replace a factual answer.

hints: Use only statements supported by the chapter.
Ignore unrelated distractors.
activities.modelAnswer: We saw there that a chain of markets links the producer of cotton to the buyer of the shirt in the supermarket. Buying and selling was taking place at every step in the chain. Markets everywhere tend to be exploitative of people - whether as workers, consumers or producers. To protect people from such exploitation, the government makes certain laws.

activities.subject: Social
activities.question: Compare two important ideas from Chapter 8.
activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.

correctItems.text: These laws try to ensure that the unfair practices are kept at a minimum in the markets.
Law and Social Justice 2024-25 101 Let us take a common market situation where the law is very important.
Private companies, contractors, businesspersons normally want to make as much profit as they can.
In the drive for profits, they might deny workers their rights and not pay them wages, for example.

Similarly to ensure that workers are not underpaid, or are paid fairly, there is a law on minimum wages.
